about: Every external source, data store, processing step and page of cosh, and the flows between them. Read by web/dataflow.html and scripts/dataflow.py (check, plan). Field meanings: docs/data-architecture.md, 'The inventory'. Keep it current: CLAUDE.md, Conventions.

groups.name: Gerrit core
groups.purpose: Code review fetched from Gerrit, reduced to per-CL and per-comment facts, labelled, and summarised for Value Exchange.

groups.name: Chromium git
groups.purpose: Chromium's git history and the patch-set commits of reviewed CLs.

groups.name: Browser usage
groups.purpose: Cloudflare Radar browser shares, the usage side of the value ratio.

groups.name: Review tone
groups.purpose: Tone scores of review comments and the Review Tone page's files.

groups.name: Review balance
groups.purpose: Per-CL author and reviewer effort, and the Review Balance page's datasets.

groups.name: Review feedback
groups.purpose: Per-person Feedback Index files, coaching reports and the review-ROI studies.

groups.name: Bugs and releases
groups.purpose: Bug-tracker metadata and Chrome Releases security fixes.

groups.name: Site
groups.purpose: Building the static site and publishing it to GitHub Pages.

sources.name: Gerrit REST
sources.purpose: CL listings (metadata, labels, accounts) per 6-hour window, and account lookups.
sources.access: Anonymous; every request carries the contact e-mail (data/private/settings.json or COSH_CONTACT).
sources.load_rules: Serial, at least 1 s apart, backoff on 429/5xx; one extractor at a time (data/private/extract.lock).
sources.coverage: chromium/src main (master before 2021-05), CLs closed 2017-W27 .. 2026-W44, plus an open-CL snapshot. Anything newer needs approval.

sources.name: Gerrit NoteDb
sources.purpose: Review comments and the full review-event history of each CL, as its refs/changes/NN/N/meta ref.
sources.access: Anonymous git over HTTPS with the contact e-mail in the user agent.
sources.load_rules: Batches of 200 explicit refspecs, one fetch at a time, at least 5 s apart, under extract.lock; more than one job only with time-limited approval.
sources.coverage: Human-owned CLs with comments, 2017-W27 .. 2026-W44, plus the open-CL snapshot's.

sources.name: Chromium affiliations file
sources.purpose: Dated e-mail-to-employer overrides used to attribute each person to an organisation.
sources.access: Anonymous GET with the contact headers.
sources.load_rules: One small request per process that builds an OrgResolver; no approval needed. COSH_AFFILIATIONS_OFFLINE=1 skips it.

sources.name: Claude (headless)
sources.purpose: Labels and scores text that rules can't: addressed threads, comment tone, AI-written descriptions, coaching reports.
sources.access: The user's Claude Max login; untrusted text only through cosh.sandbox.Sandbox (no tools, scrubbed env, bwrap jail).
sources.load_rules: Costs Max usage: size each run (--week, --max-threads, --dry-run) first. Not Gerrit load, so calls may run in parallel.
sources.coverage: Haiku for bulk labels; Opus for audits and coaching reports.

sources.name: Chromium git (shared clone)
sources.purpose: Commit history and file contents of main: commits, authors, files touched, footers, blame.
sources.access: Local reads only, always with GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1.
sources.load_rules: A clean mirror of main shared across projects: no cosh refs or local edits. No cosh command updates it.
sources.coverage: All of main with full blobs, 69 GB (2026-11-12).
sources.notes: New weeks' commits appear only after someone fetches main into the clone.

sources.name: Gerrit patch sets
sources.purpose: Every uploaded patch set (refs/changes/NN/N/*) of reviewed CLs, with blobs, for diffs between patch sets.
sources.access: Anonymous git over HTTPS with the contact e-mail.
sources.load_rules: Glob refspecs only (never ls-remote or blobs by id); up to 7 fetches at once, pausing together on a 429; under extract.lock.
sources.coverage: Reviewed CLs closed 2023-W26 .. 2026-W44: about 282k CLs, 2.0M patch sets. Older, unreviewed or newer CLs need approval.

sources.name: Cloudflare Radar
sources.purpose: Daily share of human web requests per browser (all devices, and iOS alone) and per OS.
sources.access: API token in CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, from `source ~/.secrets/cosh/secrets.sh`; never printed or committed.
sources.load_rules: Serial, at least 1 s apart; complete quarters are never refetched. A weekly update is about 3 requests.
sources.coverage: 2023-06-26 (Radar's first data) to the day of the last run.

sources.name: Chromium issue tracker
sources.purpose: Metadata (type, priority, severity, component, status) of the bugs named in commit footers and security release notes.
sources.access: Anonymous POST to an undocumented endpoint; restricted bugs are silently left out (about 46% of asked IDs are visible).
sources.load_rules: Searches serial with no wait, 50 IDs each; backs off 5/15/30 min on 429, 5xx or network errors; stops on a captcha.
sources.coverage: 147,407 bug IDs from Bug:/Fixed: footers on main since 2023-07-01 and from Chrome Releases security fixes.

sources.name: Monorail redirect stubs
sources.purpose: Redirect pages that map pre-2024 Monorail bug IDs to their new tracker IDs.
sources.load_rules: Up to 4 at once with no wait; any 429, 5xx or network error stops all workers and backs off.
sources.coverage: All 21,267 Monorail-era IDs wanted as of 2026-11-08.

sources.name: Chrome Releases blog
sources.purpose: Release posts listing each security fix's CVE, bug ID and severity.
sources.access: Anonymous GET; post bodies are parsed by regex only and never shown to a model.
sources.load_rules: Serial, at least 2 s apart, 150 posts per page; cached pages are not refetched without --refresh.

stores.purpose: Lossless cache of every Gerrit REST response, plus which weeks and open-CL snapshots are fully fetched.

tables.name: responses
tables.purpose: Every REST response, compressed, keyed by host, kind and key.

tables.name: week_progress
tables.purpose: Per ISO week: when it was listed and when all its NoteDb refs were fetched.

tables.name: week_changes
tables.purpose: Which listing response holds each CL of each week.

tables.name: open_listings
tables.purpose: Open-CL snapshots and their progress.

tables.name: open_changes
tables.purpose: Which listing response holds each CL of an open snapshot.

tables.name: extract_runs
tables.purpose: One row per extractor run: arguments, times, request count.

stores.size: 11.4 GB in 14 packs, plus 12 GB of old packs set aside
stores.files: One bare repo, chromium_src.git, with a ref refs/meta/<CL> per fetched CL (about 716k). repack-20261112/old-packs holds the packs from before the 2026-11-12 repack until a person deletes them.
stores.purpose: NoteDb history of every fetched CL: the only local copy of review comment text and review events.
stores.notes: Never prune or gc. Lossless repacks only (cosh notedb-maintain, scripts/notedb_chunked_repack.sh). Comment text is untrusted.

stores.purpose: Per-CL, per-comment, per-thread and per-commit facts without comment text; the input to nearly every analysis.

tables.name: changes
tables.purpose: One row per CL: branch, owner, status, times, close week, size, bot flag.

tables.name: comments
tables.purpose: One row per published comment by someone other than the owner on a human-owned CL: week, path, length, AI flag.

tables.name: threads
tables.purpose: Reviewer-started threads: size, owner's last reply, the regex verdict and the hash that keys labels.

tables.name: accounts
tables.purpose: Gerrit accounts: e-mail, name, bot flag.

tables.name: committers
tables.purpose: Which accounts may vote Code-Review, as of the newest listing.

tables.name: commits
tables.purpose: First-parent commits on main since 2017-07-03: CL, author, week, bot flag.

tables.name: commit_dirs
tables.purpose: Directories each commit touches, with file counts.

tables.name: meta
tables.purpose: Metric version, fetched weeks, when it was derived.

stores.notes: Rebuild: rm it, then `python3 -m cosh derive`. derived.prev.sqlite (2.1 GB) beside it is a leftover of the 2026-11-12 rebuild that no code reads.

stores.purpose: Haiku's addressed / not-addressed label for each review thread the regex doesn't settle.

tables.name: labels
tables.purpose: Addressed 0/1 per thread, classifier and input hash.

tables.name: classifiers
tables.purpose: Model, definition version and prompt hash; the newest matching the code is active.

tables.name: runs
tables.purpose: Each classify run's weeks, threads, calls, tokens and cost.

stores.notes: Covers 2022-W01 .. 2026-W44; the user doesn't want labels for 2017 .. 2021.

stores.purpose: The contact e-mail sent with every request; fetching commands fail without it.
Verbatim copy of Chromium's affiliations file, with a note of where and when it was fetched.
stores.notes: Any command that attributes orgs may rewrite it; commit it with the outputs when it changes.

stores.purpose: Hand-kept e-mail patterns that mark bot accounts and bot commit authors.
Hand-kept directory rules: which paths the contribution metrics count, and the directory tree's roots.

stores.name: Value Exchange summaries
stores.purpose: Weekly contribution by organisation, person and directory for all 487 fetched weeks: everything Value Exchange shows except usage.

tables.name: org_weekly.json
tables.purpose: Per week and org: reviewers, CLs, comments, addressed comments, commits; plus the meta block. 3.4 MB.

tables.name: weekly_totals.csv
tables.purpose: Per week: CLs merged, abandoned, by humans and bots.

tables.name: reviewer_weekly.json
tables.purpose: Every reviewer's weekly counts, for the leaderboard. 4.8 MB.

tables.name: author_weekly.json
tables.purpose: Every commit author's weekly commits. 5.0 MB.

tables.name: area_weekly.json
tables.purpose: Comments per week, directory and org. 12 MB.

tables.name: area_reviewers.json
tables.purpose: Who wrote each directory's comments. 16 MB.

tables.name: area_commits.json
tables.purpose: Commits per week, directory and org. 14 MB.

tables.name: area_authors.json
tables.purpose: Who made each directory's commits. 32 MB.

tables.name: thread_examples.json
tables.purpose: Example threads per outcome, with comment text (untrusted). 0.4 MB.

tables.name: classifier_prompt.json
tables.purpose: The addressed-classifier prompt, shown on the page.

stores.purpose: The 800-thread audit of the addressed classifier: the threads and Opus's labels, so it can be rerun.

stores.files: Bare repo with refs/patchsets/<CL>/<ps>; main's objects come from the shared clone through git alternates.
stores.purpose: Every patch-set commit of reviewed CLs with its blobs, for diffing one patch set against the next.
stores.notes: Never prune. A whole-repo repack runs out of memory: repack in groups (scripts/patchsets_chunked_repack.sh).

stores.purpose: The pilot patch-set repo: blob-less patch-set commits of 2026-W44 only, superseded by chromium-patchsets.git.
stores.notes: Read only by exploratory balance scripts. Use chromium-patchsets.git for patch sets.

stores.files: <series>_all_1d_<start>_<end>.json, one per calendar quarter, for series browser, browser_ios and os.
stores.purpose: Verbatim cache of every Radar response, committed so the share CSV can be rebuilt offline.
stores.notes: A refresh rewrites the three files of the current quarter.

stores.purpose: A one-off probe of a jump in Radar's ChromeDerivative share, behind docs/radar-research.md.
stores.notes: Written by the two scripts inside it. Nothing reads it.

stores.purpose: Each browser's weekly and monthly share of requests, with iOS removed and renormalised among Chromium browsers.
Hand-kept list of Radar's browser names: which are Chromium-based and which count in the usage denominator.
Hand-kept map from each organisation to the browsers credited to it; the page joins usage to orgs with it.
stores.notes: Config that the page reads directly, so it is also a published file.

stores.files: comments-<week>.jsonl (52 weeks), comments-sample-5pct.jsonl, gold.jsonl (tuning labels), tune-*.json, logs.
stores.purpose: Review comments rendered for tone scoring, with their thread context: one file per week and one 5% sample.
stores.notes: Holds untrusted comment text. gold.jsonl is not rebuildable. Two commands write the same week files, with and without identities.

stores.purpose: Haiku's tone score (-1 .. +1) and AI-friction flag for each scored comment.

tables.name: scores
tables.purpose: Score, AI flag and the model's reason per comment, prompt and input hash.

tables.name: prompts
tables.purpose: The prompt version, hash and model the scores were made with.

stores.notes: Per-comment reasons stay private.

stores.purpose: The tone-scoring prompts; the page shows v3.
stores.notes: Editing the current prompt changes its hash, so every comment would need rescoring.

stores.purpose: Monthly tone trend: mean score and shares of glowing, grumpy and AI-friction comments.
stores.notes: Each sentiment family has three files: committers (no suffix), .everyone and .noncommitters.

stores.purpose: Praise leaderboards and who-praises-whom counts, by person; positive totals only.
Sample comments per tone band: praise with links, negative ones anonymous after screening.
The score distribution per period, the anonymous AI-friction comments, and each person's praise comments for the name popups.
Names and e-mails of the people on the praise boards, for the page's person search.
Every commit on main with the files it touched and line counts, from the shared clone.

tables.name: gcommits
tables.purpose: Commits: author, time, CL, lines added and deleted.

tables.name: gfiles
tables.purpose: Files per commit with line counts.

tables.name: paths
tables.purpose: Path dictionary for gfiles.

stores.notes: Each balance stage file carries the whole schema, so it also has empty tables of the other stages.

stores.purpose: Each CL's patch-set uploads and attention-set changes, read from its NoteDb event log.

tables.name: uploads
tables.purpose: One row per uploaded patch set: who and when.

tables.name: attention
tables.purpose: Attention-set changes: whose turn it was and when.

tables.name: timeline_done
tables.purpose: CLs already read; a CL is never read again.

stores.purpose: Lines changed between consecutive patch sets: how much each CL was reworked during review.

tables.name: interdiff
tables.purpose: Per CL and patch-set pair: lines added and deleted, files.

stores.purpose: One wide row per CL joining the stages: author and reviewer effort, latency, rework, comments, addressed labels.

tables.name: cl
tables.purpose: Per CL: 36 columns of size, timing, review and outcome facts.

tables.name: cl_attention
tables.purpose: Per CL and person: time in the attention set.

tables.name: cl_dirs
tables.purpose: Directories each CL touches.

stores.purpose: Every Code-Review vote of each CL, read from its NoteDb event log.

tables.name: votes
tables.purpose: Vote events: who, when, value.

tables.name: votes_done
tables.purpose: CLs already read (including ones with no NoteDb ref, which are never retried).

stores.name: report inputs
stores.files: first_commit.txt (each author's first commit on main) and mech.jsonl (mechanical CLs).
stores.purpose: The side inputs most balance and feedback scripts take as --first-commit and --mech.
stores.notes: Only mech.jsonl has a command. first_commit.txt, and the owners_added.txt and narrow ai_marked.txt lists that balance scripts also take, have no script and no fixed path.

stores.purpose: Commits on main whose message marks them as AI-assisted.

stores.files: scores.sqlite (18 MB), descs.jsonl (the descriptions scored), and pilot result files.
stores.purpose: Haiku's estimate, per CL description, of whether it was AI-written.

tables.name: scores
tables.purpose: In scores.sqlite: one score per CL description.

tables.name: runs
tables.purpose: In scores.sqlite: each scoring run's cost.

stores.notes: Only scores.sqlite costs tokens to remake; the rest is rebuildable.

stores.purpose: Review-quality signals over time (vote patterns, rubber-stamp rates) for the page's monitoring section.
Contributor clusters by working pattern, with a 2-D map of them.
Per-person career reports for a few exemplar contributors; private drafts behind docs/balance-person.md.
Every dataset the Review Balance page draws, as named aggregates with no per-person rows.
stores.notes: About a dozen scripts each merge their own datasets into it, and some sections are copied in by hand. Its window ends 2026-10.

stores.purpose: Balance measures per directory, for the page's directory table.
Author-level distributions for the page's author charts.

stores.size: 126 MB (53 MB gzipped file by file, as git stores it)
stores.files: peers.json, u/<hash>.json (6,902 people, 122 other addresses) and <half-year>/<hash>.json (19 folders, 2017H2 .. 2026H2; before 2025H2 thread counts per directory, not each thread); <hash> is a salted SHA-256 of the e-mail.
stores.purpose: Per-person review feedback against peers, which the Feedback Index page fetches by a hash of the address typed.
stores.notes: Committed and published on GitHub Pages since 2026-11-12. Finished half-years' files don't change between runs unless their inputs do, so git stores them once; each run rewrites the current half-year, u/ and peers.json. Commit with `git add -A web/public/review-feedback/`.

stores.purpose: Private coaching reports that Opus writes from one person's review threads; never published.
Result files of the review-ROI studies (does review feedback predict reverts and bugs).
stores.notes: Copied here by hand from a session's scratch directory, whose path the scripts still hard-code.

stores.files: list/<month>/<n>.json.gz (2,906 search replies) and monorail/<month>/<n>.html.gz (21,267 stubs).
stores.purpose: Every tracker reply exactly as received.
stores.notes: Bug titles are untrusted: print counts and enums only.

stores.purpose: Which bugs are wanted and asked for, the request log, and the parsed metadata of visible bugs.

tables.name: wanted
tables.purpose: Bug IDs to ask for, with how many commits name each. Recomputed.

tables.name: asked
tables.purpose: Per ID: whether it was visible and when it was asked. Fetch history.

tables.name: monorail_map
tables.purpose: Old Monorail ID to new tracker ID. Fetch history.

tables.name: requests
tables.purpose: One row per HTTP request and its outcome. Fetch history.

tables.name: bugs
tables.purpose: Parsed metadata of each visible bug. Rebuildable from raw/ with `parse`.

stores.notes: Mixes fetch history that can't be rebuilt with two tables that can.

stores.files: raw/page-NNNN.json (26 feed pages), security_fixes.json, fixing_commits.json, summary.json.
stores.purpose: The Chrome Releases feed, the security fixes parsed from it, and the commits on main that fixed them.
stores.notes: Only raw/ is fetched; the three JSON files are rebuilt from it.

stores.purpose: This inventory, kept by hand whenever a source, store, step or page changes.
stores.notes: `python3 scripts/dataflow.py check` verifies it against the repository.

stores.purpose: The built site: the pages, their scripts, and a content-hashed copy of every data file a page imports.

steps.purpose: Fetches one week: lists its closed CLs over REST, fetches their NoteDb refs, then derives that week.
steps.incremental: Skips listing windows and refs already fetched; a finished week is skipped.
steps.approval: Every approval ends at 2026-W44: fetching a newer week needs the user's approval first.
steps.notes: `cosh extract --week W` fetches without deriving. The per-week derive skips the commits tables, so run a full derive afterwards.

steps.command: python3 -m cosh backfill --weeks N --newest <week> [--jobs K --jobs-until T] --go
steps.purpose: Runs the weekly fetch for many weeks, newest first.
steps.incremental: Resumable with the same command.
steps.approval: Approved and finished for 2017-W27 .. 2026-W44. Other ranges, repos or hosts need approval.
steps.notes: Long runs go in a systemd user service so they outlive the session (CLAUDE.md).

steps.purpose: Snapshots CLs that are still open (or closed after the newest fetched week), so their comments count.
steps.incremental: Each run is a new snapshot that relists the whole span; refs are fetched only when missing or stale.
steps.cost_source: No timing recorded; the 2026-11-05 run listed 47,329 CLs and fetched 5,383 refs
steps.approval: Approved; rerunning to refresh is fine, but never alongside a backfill.
steps.notes: Its default start is the oldest fetched week, now 2017-W27, so each run lists about 490 weekly windows.

steps.purpose: Copies Chromium's affiliations file into config/ when it has changed.
steps.incremental: Rewrites only on a change.
steps.notes: Rarely run by hand: summarize, review-feedback, sentiment-collect and several balance scripts run it by themselves whenever they attribute orgs (COSH_AFFILIATIONS_OFFLINE=1 stops that).

steps.purpose: Reduces every CL's listing and NoteDb comments to facts, then rebuilds the commits tables from git.
steps.incremental: Not incremental: a full run re-reads every CL. `--week W` does one week and skips commits.
steps.duration: under 52 min for 1.6M CLs; 11.5 min for 775k
steps.cost_source: File times of the 2026-11-12 run (upper bound); docs/plan.md, 2026-11-05
steps.notes: `python3 -m cosh commits` rebuilds only the commits tables (1 to 2 min). Opens raw.sqlite read-only, so it is safe beside an extractor.

steps.purpose: Has sandboxed Haiku label the threads the regex doesn't settle as addressed or not.
steps.incremental: Only threads with no label for the current classifier and input hash; saved per batch, so it resumes.
steps.duration: about 11 min per week; 41 min per year at 8 calls at once
steps.token_cost: about 0.95M Haiku tokens per week ($0.22); 25.6M per year ($6)
steps.approval: Costs Max usage: check --dry-run first (it underestimates by about a third). No labels for 2017 .. 2021.
steps.notes: A week shows the addressed metric only once it is 99% labelled, so the site's default metric needs this for each new week.

steps.purpose: Aggregates the facts and labels into the Value Exchange summaries for every fetched week.
steps.incremental: Rewrites every file for all weeks.
steps.notes: It runs update-affiliations first by itself (its only network use), so config/affiliations.json5 may change too. It reads the raw stores for the example threads' text.

steps.purpose: Lossless housekeeping of the NoteDb repo: packs refs and indexes its packs, so reads stay fast.
steps.incremental: Deletes nothing.
steps.duration: 41 min for the chunked repack of 3,823 packs into 14
steps.approval: Never prune. The chunked repack keeps the old packs until a person has checked the new ones.
steps.notes: For thousands of packs use scripts/notedb_chunked_repack.sh (700 MB groups); a whole-repo repack runs out of memory.

steps.purpose: Audits the addressed classifier against Opus, and the earlier research that chose the classifier and the Commits metric.
steps.notes: scripts/comment_classifier.py still carries an older copy of the prompt than cosh/classify.py.

steps.purpose: Fetches every patch set of reviewed CLs, newest first, into the patch-set repo.
steps.incremental: Skips CLs already fetched, even if they gained patch sets since.
steps.approval: Approved only for CLs of 2023-W26 .. 2026-W44. It has no week bound, so a plain rerun would also fetch the unapproved 2017 .. 2023 CLs.
steps.notes: Repack afterwards in groups with the two scripts; never prune.

steps.purpose: Fetches the Radar quarters that are missing or incomplete and rewrites the browser-share CSV.
steps.incremental: Complete quarters are skipped; `--offline` rebuilds the CSV from the cache alone.
steps.approval: Approved. Never print or commit the token.

steps.purpose: Renders each week's review comments with their thread context and who wrote them, ready for scoring.
steps.incremental: Rewrites the week files it is given.
steps.duration: about 25 s per week; 2 min for the 5% sample
steps.notes: `cosh.sentiment collect --sample 0.05 --name sample-5pct` makes the trend's sample. Plain `cosh.sentiment collect --week` writes the same week files without identities, which breaks praise and recent.

steps.purpose: Has sandboxed Haiku score each comment's tone and flag friction with AI.
steps.incremental: Skips comments already scored under the same prompt; saved per batch.
steps.duration: 3 to 4 min per week; 37 min for the 5% sample
steps.token_cost: about $1.25 of Haiku per week; 21.9M tokens ($5.48) for the 5% sample
steps.approval: Costs Max usage: size runs with --name or --week.

steps.purpose: Writes the monthly tone trend from the 5% sample plus the fully scored weeks.
steps.incremental: Rewrites all three files.
steps.notes: The week range is typed by hand in this and the next four commands, and must agree across them.

steps.purpose: Writes the praise leaderboards and who-praises-whom counts.
steps.incremental: Rewrites all three files.
steps.approval: Publishes names for praise only; never negative figures per person or org (docs/sentiment.md).

steps.purpose: Picks sample comments per tone band and has Haiku screen the negative ones for anything identifying.
steps.incremental: Rewrites all three files; the screening is not cached, so each run pays for it again.

steps.purpose: Writes the score distribution, the screened anonymous AI-friction comments and each person's praise comments.
steps.incremental: Rewrites all six files; the screening is not cached.

steps.purpose: Writes the names and e-mails the page's person search offers.
steps.incremental: Rewrites the file.

steps.purpose: Scores a prompt version against the 261 gold comments, to tune the prompt.
Reads every commit on main with its files and line counts.
steps.incremental: Adds commits it doesn't have.

steps.purpose: Reads each CL's uploads and attention-set changes from NoteDb.
steps.incremental: Reads only CLs not yet done; a CL updated later is not read again.

steps.purpose: Diffs each patch set against the next to measure rework during review.
steps.incremental: Only CLs without a result; CLs whose patch sets aren't fetched get none.

steps.purpose: Joins the stages into one row per CL.
steps.incremental: Rebuilds the whole table.

steps.purpose: Reads every Code-Review vote of each CL from NoteDb.
steps.incremental: Only CLs not yet done; CLs with no NoteDb ref are marked done and never retried.
steps.duration: 5 h 14 min for 631k CLs; about 30 min once NoteDb is repacked
steps.notes: A second walk of the same NoteDb logs that balance-timeline reads.

steps.purpose: Writes the list of mechanical CLs; the first-commit list beside it is made by hand from git log.
steps.incremental: Rewrites mech.jsonl.
steps.notes: mech.jsonl is written only when the BALANCE_MECH_OUT variable is set. No script writes first_commit.txt, owners_added.txt or the narrow ai_marked.txt.

steps.purpose: Lists the commits whose messages mark them as AI-assisted.

steps.command: python3 scripts/balance_ai_predict.py build && nice -n 5 python3 scripts/balance_ai_predict.py score --since 2025-07-01
steps.purpose: Has sandboxed Haiku estimate, for each CL description, whether it was AI-written.
steps.incremental: `score` resumes: descriptions already scored are skipped.
steps.duration: 116 min for 171,804 CLs at 8 calls at once

steps.command: python3 scripts/balance_report.py --first-commit F --owners-added O --ai-marked A --mech M --out report.json
steps.purpose: Computes the page's core tables; its sections and the directory table are then copied into the summaries by hand.
steps.incremental: Recomputes everything; the copy into the summaries is manual.
steps.notes: Its window is hard-coded to end 2026-10, as in every balance page script: new weeks need the constants edited.

steps.purpose: Eleven scripts that each compute a few of the page's datasets and merge them into balance.json.
steps.incremental: Each reads the file, replaces its own datasets and writes it back; nothing runs them in order.
steps.duration: 3 to 6 min each, about 40 min in all
steps.notes: Each script's exact arguments are in its docstring. balance_growth and balance_analysis still use an older rule for mechanical CLs than the rest.

steps.command: python3 scripts/balance_signals.py report ... --out data/private/balance_signals.json; python3 scripts/balance_clusters.py ...; python3 scripts/balance_cluster_map.py; python3 scripts/balance_page_extras.py
steps.purpose: Computes the review-quality signals and contributor clusters, then merges them and the security-fix totals into balance.json.
steps.incremental: Each script recomputes its own output.

steps.purpose: Writes the author-level distributions.
steps.incremental: Rewrites the file.

steps.purpose: Merges the review-ROI study results into balance.json.
steps.incremental: Replaces its own datasets in the file.

steps.command: python3 scripts/balance_analysis.py trends|growth|pipeline; scripts/balance_ai.py paired|did|footers; scripts/balance_person.py; scripts/balance_exemplars.py; scripts/balance_explore.py
steps.purpose: Exploratory analyses behind the balance docs: trends, AI effects, per-person career reports.
steps.duration: 3 to 5 min and several GB of memory each
steps.token_cost: small Haiku pilots, about $0.06 per 1,000 CLs
steps.notes: Results go into docs/balance*.md by hand. Network use is the model pilots only.

steps.purpose: Writes each person's review feedback against their peers, as files named by a hash of their address.
steps.incremental: Deletes and rewrites every file.
steps.approval: Tone is praise only. The output stays out of git until the page is published.
steps.notes: It reads main's commits before 2017 (where balance-git.sqlite starts) from the shared clone, so earlier commits count from 2008. It runs update-affiliations first by itself (its only network use). `npm run serve` picks the new files up by itself a few seconds after the run ends.

steps.purpose: Has sandboxed Opus write a private coaching report from one person's recent review threads.
steps.incremental: `--reuse` rebuilds the report from the saved reply without a new call.
steps.approval: Costs Max usage; reports are never published.

steps.command: python3 scripts/review_roi_table.py ...; review_roi_part1.py; review_roi_part2.py; review_roi_blame.py; review_roi_reverts.py; review_roi_substance.py
steps.purpose: The review-ROI studies: whether review feedback predicts later reverts, bug-fixing commits and security bugs.
steps.duration: about 1 h; the full blame runs were estimated at 10 to 16 CPU hours
steps.token_cost: Haiku pilots only: 274 tokens per thread, 200 threads
steps.notes: The scripts write to a session scratch directory they hard-code; results were copied into data/private/review_roi/ by hand. This is the only path by which bug-tracker data reaches a page.

steps.command: python3 scripts/review_impact.py --weeks 2026-W36:2026-W44 --out threads.jsonl; python3 scripts/review_impact_stats.py threads.jsonl
steps.purpose: Early study of which review threads change the CL, behind docs/review-impact.md.
Fetches the Chrome Releases feed, parses its security fixes and joins them to their fixing commits on main.
steps.incremental: Fetches only pages it lacks, so the newest page goes stale without --refresh; parse and join recompute.

steps.purpose: Lists the bug IDs to ask for, from commit footers on main and the security fixes.
steps.incremental: Recomputes the wanted table.

steps.command: nice -n 5 python3 -m cosh.bugs fetch --go && nice -n 5 python3 -m cosh.bugs monorail --go && nice -n 5 python3 -m cosh.bugs fetch --go
steps.purpose: Asks the tracker for every wanted bug not asked yet, maps old Monorail IDs, then asks for those too.
steps.incremental: Only IDs never asked; `fetch --retry-missing` re-asks invisible ones after 30 days. `parse` rebuilds the bugs table from raw/ offline.
steps.duration: about 1.5 h in all: 2,906 searches and 21,267 stub lookups
steps.approval: Approved 2026-11-08 for bugs in footers since 2023-07-01 and security fixes. Other trackers or b: bugs need approval.

steps.purpose: Builds the site: each data file a page imports gets a hashed copy, and web/public/ is copied as it is.
steps.incremental: Rebuilds everything. `npm run serve` rebuilds on change, including new pages and new files in web/public/, and serves the result on port 5182.
steps.duration: under 1 min; `npm test` adds the unit and browser tests
steps.notes: Files that no page imports never reach the site.

steps.purpose: On a push to main, builds and tests the site from the committed files and publishes it to GitHub Pages.
steps.incremental: Rebuilds the whole site in CI; it never uses a local build.
steps.notes: Runs only when web/, summaries/, the Radar CSV, config/org_browsers.csv, config/dataflow.json or the sentiment prompts change.
